newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - July 2.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - July 2.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Wednesday:
* Philippine shares were expected to consolidate within a tight range as the absence of trading incentives would keep investors at bay, brokers said.
* "The market will continue to move within a trading range of 2,900-2,760 as the market continued its consolidation," BPI Capital Corp analyst Robert Cano said.
He said investors and fund managers were still awaiting first half corporate earnings to come out before taking new positions in the market.
"Although the sentiment on corporate performance remains mixed, it is hoped that the good performance of some big-caps will push the market higher," Cano added.
He further said banking, telecommunications and property issues are good counters to consider in the near future.
* Angping & Associates analyst Audi Pantillano said the prevailing high domestic interest rates would cap any rise in share prices.
"While the market may seem moderately attractive from a valuation point of view, liquidity risks should continue to dampen any sustained rise," Pantillano said.
* On Tuesday, the Dow Jones rose 49.54 points to 7,722.33.
* The peso closed 26.374 to the dollar vs Monday's 26.376.
* The Philippine Stock Exchange composite index rises 6.33 points to 2,815.54.
* The Philippine overnight money was unchanged at 15.0625 percent.
* San Miguel Corp and Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd of Australia announce that they have completed the integration of their softdrinks operations through a $2.7 billion share swap.

* San Miguel Corp says its subsidiary San Miguel Foods Inc had closed down its 43-year old feeds plant in Manila. * Reynolds Philippines Corp says its first half operating income soared 83 percent to 60 million pesos from 32.8 million a yearago. * Ayala Land Inc's first half performance will be uninspiring but it remains the top long-term pick among Philippine property stocks, analysts say.

* The rising number of affluent Filipinos are keeping cash registers of retail shops ringing, which can boost the income of mall developer SM Prime Holdings by over 30 percent in the first half of the year, analysts say.

* APC Group says it has tied up with a major Korean group for the construction and development of its cement plant in Cebu. * Manila Times says Omico Corp expects revneues to start coming in next year as it starts pre-selling some of its property projects. -- Ramoncito dela Cruz (63 2) 841-8938 Fax 817-6267
